predecessors.name: Achaemenid Empire
predecessors.text: the satrapy of Caria, held by Hecatomnus

successors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
successors.text: Caria taken by Alexander in 334 ('Alexander captures Caria'), with Ada reinstated as its ruler; Lycia and the islands followed

ledger.x: 392: the Hecatomnids hold Caria as Persian satraps 'under the Achaemenid Empire, although they ruled with considerable autonomy'.
377: Mausolus and Artemisia move the seat from Mylasa to Halicarnassus.
355: Rhodes and the Dodecanese come under Mausolus after the Social War.
334: Alexander captures Caria (infobox 'Alexander captures Caria', undated within the page) and commits the government to Ada, who 'formally adopted Alexander as her son'.
334: Lycia and the Dodecanese pass to Alexander's sphere.
334: the Persian overlordship of Caria ends with Alexander's conquest ('Alexander captures Caria').

wars.name: Revolt of the Satraps (Mausolus on the king's side)
wars.outcome: Mausolus sided mainly with Artaxerxes and in 366 'led the siege of Adramyttium' at the king's request with Autophradates; the revolt was squashed in 362/1 and he was given Lycia.

wars.name: Social War (357-355 BC)
wars.outcome: Rhodes, Chios and Byzantium 'rebelled against Athens in 357 BCE' with Mausolus and Artemisia behind them; 'The Social War ended quickly in 355 BCE'.

wars.name: Siege of Halicarnassus
wars.outcome: Alexander captured Caria; Ada, who held Alinda, surrendered it to him and was left the government of Caria.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for the satrapy or the Dodecanese holdings; Lycia and the islands may have been lost before 334 (page silent).
